title: Day-partitioned telemetry tables

user_story.i_want: metrics, events and logs in typed tables partitioned by day
user_story.so_that: time-range queries are fast and old data is cheap to drop

description: Add a migration with schema `telemetry` and tables `metrics`, `events` and `logs` (columns per docs/architecture.md), each `PARTITION BY RANGE (occurred_at)` with `PRIMARY KEY (event_id, occurred_at)`. Each table also gets a DEFAULT partition to catch out-of-range rows, and an index on (tenant_id, name, occurred_at). A SQL function `telemetry.ensure_partitions(days_ahead int)` creates the missing daily partitions; the migration calls it for today through +7.

acceptance_criteria.then: each table has daily partitions from today to +7 plus a default partition
it lands in today's partition (checked via tableoid::regclass)

acceptance_criteria.when: it is inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

acceptance_criteria.given: a row far in the future
acceptance_criteria.then: it lands in the default partition, and a documented query counts such rows

rust_concepts: Mostly SQL: a chance to compare Postgres features with what you know from RDS
